graphrag.summary:
# Desert Locust Control Operations: 2023 vs 2024

Desert locust control operations decreased significantly from 2023 to 2024, with treated areas dropping from 11,817 hectares to 2,375 hectares—an 80% reduction. In 2023, Morocco and Saudi Arabia accounted for nearly 40% of all control operations, while 2024 saw operations spread across more countries but at substantially lower intensities. Sudan and Eritrea remained persistent problem areas in both years, though their treated acreage also declined notably (1,248 ha to 508 ha and 992 ha to 540 ha, respectively). This dramatic reduction suggests improved locust management or reduced infestation pressure in 2024 compared to the previous year.

queries.question: Which areas received rainfall that could support locust breeding?

rag.summary:
Based on the retrieved bulletins, several areas received rainfall supporting locust breeding:

# Morocco Desert Locust Activity Summary

Morocco reported locust control operations across multiple bulletins in 2023 and 2025, with a total of 2,639 hectares treated. Peak treatment activity occurred in March 2023 (B534: 857 ha), followed by February 2023 (B533: 606 ha) and June 2023 (B537: 523 ha). Lower treatment levels were documented in January 2023 (B532: 467 ha), August 2023 (B539: 66 ha), and July 2025 (B562: 120 ha). The data indicates sustained locust management efforts over an 18-month period, with the first half of 2023 representing the most intensive control operations.
